## Phase 0 — Deployability

> **Maintenance window graded per case**: the cases in this phase differ in side effects; check the "Level" column case by case.

> - BOOT-016 first creates the continuous acceptance site, and only then do BOOT-011..015, which depend on its resources, run; BOOT-017 explicitly reuses BOOT-016.
> - A formal BOOT-018 run must preserve the continuous acceptance site. BOOT-019 uses a separate uninstallable site whose CPU and GPU sides are both isolated from the protected site.
> - BOOT-020 returns to the continuous acceptance site and reads the target identity of BOOT-018, not BOOT-019; the two sites must not be mixed.
> - BOOT-021 produces formal evidence only at its own position in the order; BOOT-012 cannot issue it early.
> - BOOT-023 takes a BOOT-020 PASS as its evidence predecessor; BOOT-021/022 contain no release history for it to read.
> - BOOT-030/031 verify the two kinds of dedicated tables read-only on the continuous acceptance site, reading the evidence of BOOT-023/030 in turn. They do not change BOOT-024's BOOT-023 predecessor, nor do they authorize using the continuous acceptance site for lifecycle uninstalls.
> - BOOT-024..029 form the administrator lifecycle chain in the order remove-cluster → join-cluster re-attach → second remove and deploy bulk join → uninstall keep + reset-database → fresh deploy on empty clusters and resume; each takes the previous case's PASS as its evidence predecessor (BOOT-024 reads BOOT-023). They run only on an isolated site — that site's only GPU cluster is removed, re-attached and uninstalled as a whole; on the shared acceptance site they are recorded as BLOCKED_PREREQUISITE.
> - BOOT-029 runs cold-build first deploy → remove-cluster → join-cluster → uninstall keep + reset-database → cold-build first deploy again as one sequence driven in a single pass; it takes a BOOT-028 PASS as its evidence predecessor and requires the site installed by BOOT-028 to be uninstalled back to a pair of empty clusters first.

## Phase 5 — Remote command protocol

> Recommended to run in a maintenance window.

> - Prefer an isolated logical cluster or a test control plane; never scale the production Executor to 0 outside a maintenance window.
> - CMD-011 uses a local Executor fixture and does not rely on the control plane to inject a malformed command.
> - CMD-017 only seeds commands for the synthetic cluster perf-cap-000 and claims them with a probe executor using stand-in adapters; it injects no SXID and touches no real node.
> - CMD-018 dispatches and rewrites a step for the synthetic cluster perf-cap-000 from inside a CPU API Pod using the deployed adapter; the probe executor's action is a local ledger, and neither command has a reachable Node Agent.

## Phase 6 — Workflow preemption and DAG

> **Maintenance window graded per case**: the cases in this phase differ in side effects; check the "Level" column case by case.

> - PREEMPT-037 sets GPU_FAULT_ENABLE_WORKFLOW_DISPATCHER on gpu-fault-control-worker to false for about 10 minutes and rolls the replicas; run it only when no PENDING/RUNNING/WAITING workflow exists, it needs a maintenance window, and it must not share a window with other regional cases.
> - PREEMPT-038 writes only audit-* rows under audit-cluster to the real database, deletes them in finally, and observes the deployed periodic cleanup.

## Phase 13 — Destructive capability acceptance (including non-destructive fail-closed negative cases)

> **Maintenance window required.**

> - DESTR-025 takes a DESTR-002 PASS as its evidence predecessor and uses a device holder to produce a known reset failure on a single-node RESET_GPU workflow, proving that the linear single-node record escalates within the same record to one real RESTART_NODE and SUCCEEDED without producing a workflow-reboot-after successor; it does not disable the Agent, open a managed-recovery window or claim a spare.
> - After the ordinary DESTR-015 PASS and its cleanup complete, the physical-ownership supplementary acceptance is approved separately and runs in the order unchanged-owner, ownership-drift, late-sibling; it uses an independent, non-nested run-dir and does not overwrite the ordinary case evidence. It is attributed to DESTR-015 as a whole, and PREEMPT-033 only references the same set of mechanism evidence; it must not be inserted into phase-6 or repeat the physical trial under an alias. --ordinary-destr015-evidence explicitly binds the success and cleanup result of the original ordinary case, and --predecessor-evidence still keeps the DESTR-012 predecessor proof.
> - DESTR-023 takes a DESTR-001 PASS as its evidence predecessor and performs another real GPU reset on a truly idle cluster with no managed job, all observation streams expired and only the watcher coverage heartbeat left, proving the node is not BLOCKED because of UNKNOWN; it changes no control-plane or watcher setting.
> - DESTR-024 takes a DESTR-023 PASS as its predecessor, scales the completion watcher to 0 so the heartbeat expires, injects the same XID 46, and allows only FREEZE/MARK_UNSCHEDULABLE/QUARANTINE and BLOCKED with no quiesce, no reset and no reboot; a detached watchdog restores the watcher as a backstop, and isolation is lifted only through the validated restore workflow.
> - DESTR-020 takes a DESTR-001 PASS as its evidence predecessor and replays an out-of-catalog XID through the API against an alias node_id unknown to both Kubernetes and the fleet (a SITE_SAFETY isolation plan with no physical step), proving only that MARK_UNSCHEDULABLE fails closed on 404; the alias has neither a Node Agent nor a provider node, so no reset/reboot can possibly be armed; support escalation happens exactly once (containment_refused, only FREEZE_EVIDENCE→ESCALATE_SUPPORT), chain depth ≤1.
> - DESTR-021 takes a DESTR-020 PASS as its evidence predecessor, reuses the EFA unbind injection of COLLECT-017 segment A, and runs the seven-step EFA recovery under a pre-written stale foreign plugin-restart annotation and local concurrent tick annotation writes; no reset, no reboot, no replace.
> - The refutation that the provider replace switch is off is carried by DESTR-013 at the end of the phase (the former DESTR-011 has been merged in, see do_not_run); DESTR-005..007 only construct steps in an isolated process and do not depend on that refutation running first.
> - DESTR-009 must run before DESTR-012.
> - DESTR-012 sub-cases run strictly in the order B, A, D, C.
> - DESTR-015 takes a DESTR-012 PASS as its predecessor (and also depends on DESTR-001's real reset and DESTR-009's job restart each having been established); each of the two nodes performs one real GPU reset, with no reboot.
> - DESTR-016 takes a DESTR-002 PASS as its predecessor; at the VERIFY_NO_GPU_CLIENTS barrier of RESET_GPU it first absorbs one same-rank XID 46, then XID 79 preempts to RESTART_NODE, authorizing only one provider reboot.
> - DESTR-017 takes a DESTR-002 PASS as its predecessor and reboots the node once through an out-of-band systemd timer while RESET_GPU waits, calling no provider action.
> - DESTR-018 takes a DESTR-010 PASS as its predecessor and opens a temporary environment window on the CPU-side gpu-fault-control-worker that compresses GPU_FAULT_NODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS and GPU_FAULT_WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS to 180 s; the window opens before injection and closes after quiescence, and it must not share a window with other regional cases.
> - DESTR-019 takes a DESTR-010 PASS as its evidence predecessor and restarts the Node Agent once, only while no remote command is in flight (arming a fail-safe start first), then runs DESTR-010's two-step XID 45 workflow to check the audit trail; no reset/reboot/isolation.

## Phase 14 — Warm spare

> **Maintenance window required.**

> - DESTR-003 takes a DESTR-012 PASS as its evidence predecessor (the warm-spare switch happens only after job-recovery ownership is established) and does not read DESTR-021's evidence.
> - DESTR-022 takes a DESTR-008 PASS as its evidence predecessor and writes a stale reservation for a synthetic incident on the hot spare still claimed by 003/008, then only waits for the deployed executor's sweep to reclaim it by TTL; the hot spare stays cordoned throughout, no workflow is triggered, and it must run before DESTR-014 returns the spare.
> - DESTR-014 claims no warm spare (what it wants is precisely for REPLACE_NODE to fail for lack of a hot spare); before it runs, the claimed spare must first be returned with DESTR-003's --release.
> - DESTR-014 contains two real BatchRebootClusterNodes calls and must run before DESTR-013 so that they fall inside the CloudTrail window DESTR-013 covers.

## Phase 16 — Multiple physical clusters

> **Maintenance window required.**

> Prerequisite: at least two enabled physical GPU clusters

> - E2E-002 takes an ISO-001 PASS as its evidence predecessor: ISO-001 is the single-injection isolation case for the same identity and E2E-002 is its two-injection successor; ISO-006 (whole cluster offline) proves something E2E-002 does not depend on, so ISO-006's evidence is not read.
> - ISO-007 reuses the same physical cluster pair to verify that A's explicit zero-budget denial does not block B's one successful recovery; the real workload restart needs a maintenance window.

## Phase 17 — Collection and decision coverage

> **Maintenance window graded per case**: the cases in this phase differ in side effects; check the "Level" column case by case.

> - COLLECT-021 takes a COLLECT-016 PASS as its evidence predecessor: it reuses COLLECT-016's managed training fixture and host probe to verify that the race where the Pod dies first and the RESTART_APP XID arrives later is judged MONITOR_ONLY while the passive path still restarts; it is ordered after COLLECT-016.
> - COLLECT-015 takes a COLLECT-017 PASS as its evidence predecessor (the run_collector_destructive.py chain); COLLECT-018..020 are ordered before it only so that the reboot happens last.
> - The formal predecessor of COLLECT-009 is COLLECT-005: COLLECT-006/007 are pytest cases and produce no cases/<id>/<id>.json evidence.
> - COLLECT-004's expected-count alternative path triggers a real HyperPod reboot and must run in a maintenance window.
> - The last six cases involve a reset, EFA mutation, workload restart or reboot and must run in a maintenance window.
> - COLLECT-018/019/020 open a bounded collector window on one idle node (synthetic API injection, nvidia-smi shadow, drop-in environment) without touching the GPUs; COLLECT-020 cordons that node for DCGM diagnostics and then restores it through validation-first restore, needs a maintenance window, and is still ordered before COLLECT-015's reboot.

## Phase 18 — Full uninstall of an isolated site

> **Maintenance window required.**

> - Operate only on a disposable site that was deployed independently in advance and carries this case's ownership label; do not uninstall the continuous acceptance site.
> - The first run returns RESTART_REQUIRED after the native Kubernetes cleanup verification; a new process resumes under the same approval, and nothing may proceed before the final PASS.
> - CPU cluster deletion, the final Aurora snapshot, GPU cluster retention and the unchanged continuous site must all be verified; API unreadability cannot stand in as proof of deletion.
